description: Fine-tuning + parameter-efficient methods decomposed. Full fine-tuning, LoRA, QLoRA, Adapters, Prefix tuning, P-tuning. The mechanisms by which large pretrained models are specialised to tasks at fraction of pretraining cost.

sub_mechanisms.name: full_fine_tuning
sub_mechanisms.definition: Continue training all weights on task-specific data. Smaller learning rate than pretraining.
sub_mechanisms.why: Strongest adaptation. Cost: all weights changed; storage of fine-tuned model = full base model size. Need lots of memory; not practical for 70B+ models on consumer GPUs.

sub_mechanisms.name: LoRA_decomposition
sub_mechanisms.definition: Add low-rank matrices: W_new = W_frozen + A @ B where A is (d, r) and B is (r, d), r small. Train only A, B.
sub_mechanisms.why: Hypothesis: task-specific change is low-rank. r=4-32 typical. Train ~0.1-1% of params. Result: full-quality fine-tune with tiny memory overhead.

sub_mechanisms.name: LoRA_rank_parameter
sub_mechanisms.definition: r controls capacity of adaptation. Too low: undercapacity. Too high: overfits + more memory.
sub_mechanisms.why: Empirical sweet spot for LLM tasks: r=8-32. Rank 4 sometimes works for instruction tuning. Higher ranks for very different tasks.

sub_mechanisms.name: LoRA_alpha_scaling
sub_mechanisms.definition: Effective change = (α/r) × A @ B. α decouples adaptation strength from rank.
sub_mechanisms.why: Lets rank + strength be tuned independently. α = r common default; α = 2r more aggressive. Subtle hyperparameter that matters.

sub_mechanisms.name: LoRA_target_modules
sub_mechanisms.definition: Apply LoRA to specific layer types: Q, K, V projections; sometimes MLP. All linear layers possible.
sub_mechanisms.why: Targeted LoRA on attention often beats spread-thin LoRA on everything. Standard: Q + V, or Q + K + V. Experimentation needed per task.

sub_mechanisms.name: LoRA_merging
sub_mechanisms.definition: After training: W_final = W_frozen + A @ B. Merge into weights for inference; no LoRA overhead.
sub_mechanisms.why: Inference uses standard linear layers. Cost: lose ability to swap LoRAs. Alternative: keep separate at inference to swap multiple adapters.

sub_mechanisms.name: QLoRA
sub_mechanisms.definition: LoRA on 4-bit quantised base model. Tim Dettmers 2023. Train 65B model on single 48GB GPU.
sub_mechanisms.why: Combines quantisation + LoRA. Base weights in 4-bit (frozen, but used in forward); LoRA in fp16 (trained). Massive memory savings. Standard for consumer-GPU fine-tuning.

sub_mechanisms.name: adapter_modules
sub_mechanisms.definition: Houlsby 2019. Insert small MLP blocks between transformer layers. Train only adapters.
sub_mechanisms.why: Pre-LoRA parameter-efficient method. Adds latency (extra layers). Largely superseded by LoRA which doesn't add inference cost.

sub_mechanisms.name: prefix_tuning
sub_mechanisms.definition: Learn prefix tokens prepended to input. Frozen model attends to them.
sub_mechanisms.why: Tunes attention behaviour without changing weights. Particularly small footprint. Quality lower than LoRA on hard tasks.

sub_mechanisms.name: catastrophic_forgetting_in_fine_tune
sub_mechanisms.definition: Fine-tuning teaches new task but model forgets pretraining knowledge.
sub_mechanisms.why: Standard problem. Mitigations: replay old examples, EWC (penalise weight changes), LoRA (only adapters change, base frozen). LoRA's structural prevention is part of its appeal.

sub_mechanisms.name: instruction_tuning_pipeline
sub_mechanisms.definition: Fine-tune base model on (instruction, response) pairs. Usually with LoRA. Often followed by DPO/RLHF.
sub_mechanisms.why: Bridges raw pretraining (next-token) to chat (instruction-following). Standard for shipping LLMs. Datasets: Alpaca, Dolly, OpenAssistant, ShareGPT.

sub_mechanisms.name: PEFT_library_huggingface
sub_mechanisms.definition: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning library: LoRA, QLoRA, IA³, prefix tuning unified API.
sub_mechanisms.why: Standard tooling. Wrap base model + adapter config = trainable PEFT model. Adapter checkpoints small (~MB) — easy to share.

derivation_rules.name: task_adaptation_is_low_rank
if: fine-tuning task is similar to pretraining
then: the weight change has low intrinsic rank
derivation_rules.why: Empirical observation behind LoRA. Pretrained model already encodes general capabilities; task-specific tuning is a small perturbation. Rank 8-32 captures it for most LLM tasks.

derivation_rules.name: LoRA_memory_advantage
if: LoRA with rank r applied to (d, d) layer
then: trainable params drop from d² to 2dr (typically 100-1000x reduction)
derivation_rules.why: d² params in dense layer; 2dr in LoRA. d=4096, r=8: 16M params → 64K params. 250x reduction. Plus: optimiser state (Adam: 2x param) scales with trainable params. Total memory savings ~250x.

derivation_rules.name: QLoRA_enables_consumer_GPU_finetuning
if: base model in 4-bit + LoRA in fp16
derivation_rules.why: 70B fp32: 280 GB. 70B fp16: 140 GB. 70B int4: 35 GB. + LoRA + activations: ~45 GB. Tim Dettmers' QLoRA showed this is possible. Democratised LLM fine-tuning.

derivation_rules.name: LoRA_prevents_catastrophic_forgetting
if: base weights are frozen during fine-tuning
derivation_rules.why: Full fine-tuning may overwrite useful patterns. LoRA's frozen base means general capabilities can't be forgotten; only the additive change captures task. Architectural prevention.

derivation_rules.name: merged_LoRA_no_inference_cost
if: LoRA matrices merged into base weights after training
then: inference cost equals base model (no overhead)
derivation_rules.why: W + AB is just a matrix; same shape as W. Inference uses single matmul. LoRA's deployment story: train tiny + merge or swap. Adapters add inference latency; LoRA doesn't.
